title: CAP Theorem

searches.query: "CAP Theorem" system design interview partition PACELC
searches.result: success; exact-concept search executed, but independent frequency/rank/company evidence was insufficient; prompts are original production adaptations and technical decisions use checked primary sources

sources.title: Gilbert and Lynch: Brewer’s Conjecture (2002)
sources.supportRationale: Original asynchronous-model impossibility result and precise atomic consistency/availability definitions; an inaccessible MIT URL was replaced by the author's copy.

sources.title: Gilbert and Lynch: Perspectives on the CAP Theorem
sources.supportRationale: Original authors' explanation of safety/liveness and practical partition trade-offs.

sources.title: Abadi: Consistency Tradeoffs in Modern Distributed Database System Design
sources.supportRationale: PACELC distinguishes partition-time availability/consistency from ordinary replication latency/consistency trade-offs; historical product labels are not reused as current guarantees.

sources.title: etcd v3.6: API guarantees
sources.supportRationale: Explicit v3.6 KV consistency, weaker serializable read option, watch limitations and lease behavior.

scenarios.theme: An isolated region misses a global kill switch. What promise can you keep?
scenarios.assumptions: The product wants every action after acknowledged disable to be rejected, even in a region that cannot communicate. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.
